To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Treistman-Brezin-Eynard-Mariano (TBEM) eigenvalue matrix models, which represent the colored HOMFLy polynomials for toroidal knots as averages of characters, can be generalized to a class of knots, which includes the trefoil, and that the measure of such a matrix model is provided by a Laplace evolution on the Jones polynomial.

the TBEM matrix model is provided by the Laplace evolution of the Jones polynomial, and this evolution is a special case of the Laplace flow for Hurwitz τ-functions, which is known to be related to the cut-and-join equation.

the Treister-Brini-Eynard-Marino (TBEM) eigenvalue matrix models, representing the non-normalized HOMFLY polynomial for torus knots, can be generalized to the family of twist knot polynomials, but the generalization is not a simple one and requires a nontrivial deformation of the TBEM matrix model.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question: is there a natural generalization of the TBEM matrix model to non-torus knots, which could be a basis for a generalization of the matrix model approach to the representation of HOMLY polynomials?
the problem of matrix model representation of the HOMFLY invariants, and we present a partial solution, which works well for the trefoil and torus knots, but fails to be a generalization of the TBEM.
the problem of constructing a matrix model for HOMFLY polynomial for arbitrary knot.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the matrix model representation of colored HOMFLYY polynomials is a very interesting problem, which deserves a further attention and investigation.
, at least for the trefoil, the TBEM matrix model provides an exact representation for the colored HOMFLYY polynomials in terms of the Jones polynomial.

the TBEM matrix model is not an appropriate tool to describe the N = 1 HOMFLY for the twist knots, and that it can be used only as an intermediate step in the construction of a matrix model for the N =2 HOMFLY.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while the TBEM-like integral representations of HOMFLy polynomials are possible, they are rather limited in their scope and applicability.
the TBEM model is a special case of a more general class of models, which can be obtained from a certain deformation of the Hurwitz τ-functions.
the TBEM-like matrix model is a natural candidate for a representation of the HOMFLY polynomial in a matrix model language, which is a generalization of the Kontsevich matrix model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TBEM-like models are not unique and there exist other models of the same type.
the TBEM matrix model is not a unique way of representing the colored HOMFLYY polynomials, but rather a particular choice in a class of models, which are related by the Laplace evolution.
, in contrast to the TBEM case, the measure of the Laplace-evolved model is not a simple product of characters, but a more complicated combination.
